assertion: Among tenants represented by a CLCPP attorney for their entire case, the percentage who stayed in their homes decreased from 77% in 2022 through 2024 to 63% in the first half of 2026
why_not: The page 19 passage shows the 77% baseline is the share of ALL cases with known outcomes ending in tenant possession (Jan 2022-Dec 2024), not full-representation cases only. That supports the grade: the 63% (319 of 508 closed cases with known outcomes, Jan-Jun 2026) is the same all-case measure, so the article misdescribes the population. The numbers themselves match.
independent_value: CLCPP Jan-Jun 2026 report: tenants retained possession in 319 of 508 closed cases with known outcomes (63%), across all service levels. The Jul-Dec 2025 report gives the 77% baseline for all cases with known outcomes.

assertion: Since 2022, CLCPP data show that 73% of the cases that were dismissed because a tenant paid their back rent used ERAP to help do so. In the first half of 2026, it was 32%.
independent_value: CLCPP reports: ERAP involved in 73% of payment dismissals Jan 2022-Dec 2024; 32% in Jan-Jun 2026.

assertion: In the first half of 2026, landlords were represented by attorneys in 93% of 1,487 active eviction cases involving CLCPP clients who had been served with a complaint. Of the eviction cases CLCPP closed during that period, only 12% of tenants had an attorney representing them throughout their case. (Another 17% received legal representation for part of their case).
independent_value: Report: landlord represented in 1,363 of 1,487 (92%) in Jan-Jun 2026; the 93% figure is the cumulative 2019-2026 rate. Full representation 12%, limited scope 17% of 1,739 closed cases: correct.
